lines.trans: Cindy's agency keeps saying there will be no issue with the next shoot, yet to my eyes it is asking too much.
So let us think up a backup plan, like bringing in a guest just for that day.
There is a rumor that event fell through—they say Cindy never got on the plane.
All the reporters waiting out there to shoot her airport fashion came up empty-handed.
Cindy's hospital discharge photos already went up all over the internet—did she go into hiding?
What are you doing?
I am sorry!
Come on, does that make any sense? Think about what kind of woman CEO Byun is!
Cindy lives right in the palm of CEO Byun's hand—even if she disappeared, she has nowhere to go.

meanings.note: Basic verb of motion. With the respectful ending -세요 in 안녕히 가세요, it forms the polite farewell 'Goodbye!'. RR: gada.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그 아이 ('that child/kid'); used only for younger people or close peers.

examples.trans: Are you close with her?
He is late every day.

related.gloss: this kid / he or she (near speaker)
that kid / he or she (over there)

meanings.note: Points to a place near the listener, and in casual or brisk speech is used to call out to someone whose name you do not know. RR: geogi.

examples.trans: Hey, you there, just a moment!
How is the atmosphere there?

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.en: guest (especially on a TV or radio show)
meanings.note: Loanword from English 'guest', commonly used in broadcasting.

examples.trans: Who is the guest on today's broadcast?
We invited a special guest.

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Is the teacher inside right now?

meanings.note: Used as noun (공항).

examples.text: 예, 실장님 연락처 받았습니다. 공항 도착하는 대로 바로 연락드리겠습니다.
examples.trans: Yes, Director, I got the contact info. I will call you the moment we arrive at the airport.

examples.text: 공항 패션 찍는다고 나가 있던 기자들 다 물 먹었대.
examples.trans: All the reporters waiting out there to shoot her airport fashion came up empty-handed.

meanings.note: refers to something known to both speakers or near the listener

examples.trans: That movie was really fun.
What is that person's name?

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그것

examples.trans: Where did you buy that?
That is a really good idea.

meanings.note: refers to a previously mentioned or specific day

examples.trans: We have lots of stages that day.
I don't have time that day.

meanings.note: adverb therefore

examples.trans: So let's go.
Therefore it is good.

meanings.note: A person who gathers and reports news.

examples.trans: My dream is to become a reporter.
The reporters asked many questions.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

나가다.gloss: to go out, to step outside

meanings.en: to go out, to step outside, to leave a room
meanings.note: 나- ('out') + 가다 ('to go')

examples.trans: Let's step outside for a moment and talk.
He went out of the conference room.

meanings.en: to arise, to come up, to occur
meanings.note: Used with feelings, thoughts, or events (e.g. 실감이 나다, 생각이 나다).

examples.trans: A good idea came to mind.
Tears suddenly came to my eyes.
I want to put in right now.
How about trying to put in together tomorrow?

meanings.en: video recording, television taping or shoot
meanings.note: Often paired with 하다 (녹화하다, 'to record/tape').

examples.trans: There is a shoot this afternoon.
The taping finished late.

meanings.note: Placed before the verb it modifies.

examples.trans: I finished all my homework.
I ate all the rice.

meanings.note: Used for time or order.

examples.trans: Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.

meanings.note: Used as noun + object (대안을).

examples.text: 그러니까 그날만 게스트를 넣든 대안을 생각해보자고.
examples.trans: So let us think up a backup plan, like bringing in a guest just for that day.
This point about an alternative is really important.
He is our company's president.
I will speak as the representative.

meanings.note: Bound noun referring to a location.

examples.trans: I have no place to go.
I have no place to go. (2)

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: Often used as a bound noun after -(으)ㄹ to mean 'when' or 'while'.

examples.trans: Call me when you have time.
I lived in this neighborhood when I was young.

meanings.note: colloquial broadcast/media usage, as in 녹화를 뜨다

examples.text: 사전 녹화 좀 떠주면 안 되냐?
examples.trans: Couldn't your side pre-record them for us?
We recorded the stage footage in advance.

meanings.note: Combines with 하다 in 말하다 (to speak, to say).

examples.trans: I don't know what you mean.
You speak Korean well.

meanings.note: Everyday verb for eating a meal or food; honorific equivalent is 드시다.

examples.trans: Let's eat lunch together.
Did you eat breakfast?

meanings.note: Used as noun + casual copula (무리야.).

examples.text: 신디네 회사에서는 다음 녹화 지장 없겠다 어쩌고 하는데 내가 봤을 땐 무리야.
examples.trans: Cindy's agency keeps saying there will be no issue with the next shoot, yet to my eyes it is asking too much.
This point about it is unreasonable is really important.

examples.text: 이 스프레이로 물 뿌리고 신디가 깨면 까나리카노를 내밀면 돼.
examples.trans: Spray water with this bottle, and when Cindy wakes up, hand her this fish-sauce coffee.
The topic of water came up during this shoot.

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

meanings.note: Used as noun + object (비행기를).

examples.text: 거기 펑크 났다는 소문이 있어요. 신디가 비행기를 안 탔대요.
examples.trans: There is a rumor that event fell through—they say Cindy never got on the plane.
This point about the airplane is really important.

meanings.note: Pairs with the verb 찍다 ('to take/snap') in 사진을 찍다.

examples.trans: Shall we take a photo together?
This photo came out really well!

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 잘 생각해보세요, 저런 여자가 의외로 진국일 수가 있다니까.
examples.trans: Give it serious thought—a woman like her can turn out to be the real deal.
This expression comes from 'think it over'.
Is that rumour true?
A strange rumour is going around the company.

meanings.note: Used as noun (손바닥).

examples.text: 신디 걔는 변 대표 손바닥 안이야. 걔는 잠적해도 갈 데가 없어요.
examples.trans: Cindy lives right in the palm of CEO Byun's hand—even if she disappeared, she has nowhere to go.
This point about palm of the hand is really important.

meanings.en: earlier, a short while ago (same day)

examples.trans: I called earlier.
What did you say earlier?

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)

meanings.note: Casual exclamation used to call someone younger or a close friend.

examples.trans: Hey, come quickly!
Hey, where are you going?

meanings.en: to be how, to be in what state
meanings.note: Its adverbial form 어떻게 ('how') is used to ask how something is done or how things turned out.

examples.trans: How do you feel today?
How did the meeting turn out?

meanings.note: Used as colloquial adverb (어쩌고).

examples.text: 신디네 회사에서는 다음 녹화 지장 없겠다 어쩌고 하는데 내가 봤을 땐 무리야.
examples.trans: Cindy's agency keeps saying there will be no issue with the next shoot, yet to my eyes it is asking too much.
I thought it over again (blah blah, and so on).

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.
Did you hear about this female?
I was busy today because of female.

meanings.note: Used as noun + locative (인터넷에).

examples.text: 신디 퇴원 사진은 아까 인터넷에 다 떴어요. 잠적한 거 아니야?
examples.trans: Cindy's hospital discharge photos already went up all over the internet—did she go into hiding?

examples.text: 그냥 핸드폰 꺼놓고 인터넷 하루 안 했을 뿐인데 그것만으로도 되게 좋더라고요, 시간도 많이 생기고.
examples.trans: All I did was switch off my phone and stay off the internet for one day, yet that alone felt wonderful and freed up so much time.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.note: Used as past adnominal (잠적한).

examples.text: 신디 퇴원 사진은 아까 인터넷에 다 떴어요. 잠적한 거 아니야?

meanings.note: Respectful, polite adjective used to apologize in workplaces and to strangers. Formal 죄송합니다 is the standard workplace apology. RR: joesonghada.

examples.trans: I am very sorry for being late.
I am sorry for the inconvenience.

meanings.note: Used as noun (지장).

examples.text: 신디네 회사에서는 다음 녹화 지장 없겠다 어쩌고 하는데 내가 봤을 땐 무리야.
examples.trans: Cindy's agency keeps saying there will be no issue with the next shoot, yet to my eyes it is asking too much.
This point about hindrance, problem is really important.

meanings.en: to film, to shoot, to take (a photo)
meanings.note: Used for capturing photos or video.
Also means to stamp a seal or dip food into sauce.

examples.trans: Did you happen to film this just now too?
May I take a photo here?

meanings.note: intransitive verb; also means 'to ride' in another sense

examples.text: 불을 줄이지 않으면 고기가 다 타요.
examples.trans: If you don't lower the heat, the meat will burn completely.
Firewood is burning brightly in the stove.

meanings.note: Used as noun (퇴원).

examples.text: 신디 퇴원 사진은 아까 인터넷에 다 떴어요. 잠적한 거 아니야?
examples.trans: Cindy's hospital discharge photos already went up all over the internet—did she go into hiding?
This point about hospital discharge is really important.

meanings.note: Used as noun (패션).

examples.text: 공항 패션 찍는다고 나가 있던 기자들 다 물 먹었대.
examples.trans: All the reporters waiting out there to shoot her airport fashion came up empty-handed.
This point about fashion is really important.
Did you hear about this sudden cancellation?
I was busy today because of sudden cancellation.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.
My office is close to home.
I go to work at the office at 9 a.m.
